newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARLINS RALLY FOR DRAMATIC 13-INNING WIN OVER ASTROS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARLINS RALLY FOR DRAMATIC 13-INNING WIN OVER ASTROS.

text.p: Moises Alou's RBI single with two out in the top of the 13th inning capped a dramatic come-from-behind 9-8 victory for the Florida Marlins over the Houston Astros on Saturday.

Kurt Abbott and Gary Sheffield singled with two out in the 13th off Ramon Garcia (2-1) to put runners on the corners. Alou followed with a bouncer that glanced off third baseman Sean Berry's glove, allowing Abbott to score the winning run as the Marlins snapped a 10-game road losing streak.
Florida trailed 8-6 entering the ninth inning but forced the game into extra innings when Gregg Zaun and Abbott belted solo home runs off reliever John Hudek in the ninth.
Felix Heredia (2-0) notched the victory with a scoreless 12th. He allowed three hits in the inning, but got a pair of strikeouts to escape a jam.
Garcia surrendered one run and three hits for Houston, which stranded seven men in scoring position from the seventh inning on.
In New York, Carl Everett and Todd Hundley each drove in two runs and Carlos Baerga went 4-for-4 as the Mets beat the St Louis Cardinals 5-1.
The Mets have won six of their last seven games and 10 of 15 to get within a game of .500 (14-15).
Rick Reed (3-1), who set down the first 12 batters he faced, gave up one run and six hits with no walks and six strikeouts to win his third straight start.
John Olerud homered in the fourth for the Mets and has seven RBI in his last six games. Hundley whacked a solo homer, his seventh, off Andy Benes (1-1) in the sixth to make it 3-1.
At Colorado, Jamey Wright pitched seven strong innings and Eric Young had two doubles and two RBI to lead the Rockies to a 7-3 win over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Wright (4-1) limited Philadelphia two runs and four hits with four walks and four strikeouts as the Rockies won for the ninth time in their last 12 games.

Philadelphia starter Mark Portugal (0-2) left after three innings with tenderness in his right elbow after giving up two runs and four hits with four walks. Philadelphia pitchers issued nine walks and four of those runners scored.
In San Francisco, John Smiley scattered seven hits over seven shutout innings and Lenny Harris's squeeze in the top of the eighth scored the go-ahead run as the Cincinnati Reds beat the Giants 3-1.
Deion Sanders added an RBI double and Hal Morris lifted a sacrifice fly in the ninth for Cincinnati.
Smiley (2-5) snapped a personal five-game losing streak, winning for the first time since Opening Day. He did not walk a batter and struck out eight.
In Atlanta, Esteban Loaiza and Ricardo Rincon combined on a four-hit shutout as the Pittsburgh Pirates won their third in a row with a 3-0 victory over the Atlanta Braves.
Loaiza gave up four hits and walked two with three strikeouts in eight innings and Rincon notched his second save with a hitless ninth.

Jeff Blauser went 3-for-3 and Michael Tucker had the only other hit for the Braves. Tom Glavine (4-1) retired the first 12 batters he faced but took the loss, despite allowing just one run and five hits.
In San Diego, Tim Worrell and Trevor Hoffman combined on a three-hitter and Tony Gwynn homered as the Padres blanked the Montreal Expos 1-0.
Worrell (2-3) allowed three hits, walked one and struck out eight over 7 2/3 innings. Hoffman struck out the side in the ninth for his fourth save.
Gwynn belted his seventh homer in the first inning off Montreal starter Dustin Hermanson for the game's lone run.

In Los Angeles, Terry Mulholland came within one out of his first shutout in four years and the Chicago Cubs scored two unearned runs to snap a three-game losing streak with a 2-1 victory over the Dodgers.
Mulholland (2-3) gave up six hits for the win.
Dave Hansen and Brian McRae had run-scoring singles for the Cubs, who broke a five-game road losing streak.
Ismael Valdes (1-4) gave up two unearned runs and five hits in 7 2/3 innings while striking out a seven as the Dodgers saw their four-game winning streak halted.
